Subject: Control Plane & Private Endpoint Egress — inventory and allowlist action items

Marissa / Aditya —

EdgeWorks is validating outbound controls for their private deployment (VPC + dedicated control-plane connector). Security has asked for a compact inventory of all outbound endpoints that the control plane and private connectors may need to talk to, with IPs, FQDNs, ports, and which flow (control plane vs. data plane) each applies to. They've also requested a short summary of our recommended firewall rules and an explanation of any transient egress ranges (eg. for autoscaling, third-party metrics, or package updates).

Can we turn around an initial inventory + ruleset by EOD today so I can send to EdgeWorks security? Priorities:
- Single CSV with IP/FQDN/port/protocol/provider/purpose
- Mark which are mandatory vs optional (monitoring, telemetry, updates)
- Call out any dynamic ranges and how customers can mitigate (eg. egress gateway, NAT pool pinning)
- Attach brief one-page supporting note (one PDF) describing our reasoning and recommended firewall policy statements

I attached the partial inventory we have from the on-prem pilot (egress-ip-inventory.csv). Aditya — can you complete the connector-specific rows (control plane callbacks, metrics, artifact fetch) and add notes about retries/backoff? Marissa — can you confirm the monitoring/telemetry endpoints and whether they can be proxied via customer-managed outbound proxies?

Thanks — I know this is a quick turnaround but EdgeWorks has a compliance review window this afternoon.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: egress-ip-inventory.csv (csv, 12KB)

Subject: Re: Control Plane & Private Endpoint Egress — inventory and allowlist action items

Olga —

Working on it. Quick notes and gaps so we don't miss anything for EdgeWorks: 

1) Control plane callbacks:
   - Primary: control.redwood-api.relay.redwood.ai -> 52.14.23.110:443 (AWS ELB) — mandatory
   - Fallback: control-alt.relay.redwood.ai -> 3.229.45.66:443 (multi-az) — mandatory for HA

2) Connector artifact fetches (models & weights):
   - models-prod.s3.redwood.ai -> S3 ranges vary by region; recommend customers allow *.s3.redwood.ai and pin to our CDN IPs if possible. For EdgeWorks (us-east-1) provide exact IP CIDRs — see CSV.

3) Telemetry & metrics:
   - metrics.ingest.redwood.ai:443 (TLS) — optional to allow; can be proxied to customer SIEM
   - heartbeat: connector-ping.redwood.ai:443 — mandatory every 60s by default; we can lengthen to 5m for bandwidth-constrained networks

4) TLS and SNI: all our endpoints use TLS with SNI. Customers who only allow IPs will need to permit the IPs + enforce SNI at their perimeter to avoid breaking multi-tenant endpoints.

I've populated the CSV with the above and included notes on NAT amplification and autoscaling: our outbound NAT pool is dynamic when connectors scale out; recommendation is either:
  - Customer-managed NAT with pinned elastic IPs (preferred), or
  - Use our egress gateway feature (we publish a stable egress IP block) if customer cannot manage NAT.

I'll attach the updated CSV and a short PDF with the recommended firewall statements.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: egress-ip-inventory.csv (updated, 18KB), redwood-private-connector-network-digest.pdf (1 page)

Thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifying Qs from our side: 

1) For model artifact fetches: can you provide the exact CIDR(s) for the CDN/edge nodes you expect connectors to pull from in us-east-1? Allowing *.s3.redwood.ai is not acceptable for us.

2) Heartbeat/health-check frequency — our compliance baseline prefers 5m heartbeats for third-party connectors. You mentioned this can be changed; what are the trade-offs to set 5m? Any impact on failover detection?

3) Package updates & apt/yum repos — do your connectors reach out to external package repositories at deploy time? If yes, can that be proxied to an internal package proxy?

4) Confirmation that the egress gateway IP block you publish will be stable for 90 days once we accept it (we need to rotate ipsec and firewall rules on a quarterly cadence).

If you can reply with the CIDRs and a short note on heartbeat trade-offs we'll be able to move this to our network team for sign-off.

Best,
EdgeWorks Security Team

Alice / EdgeWorks team —

Thanks for the questions. Short answers below and next steps at the bottom. Full CIDRs and a one-page rationale are attached.

1) CDN / artifact CIDRs (us-east-1):
   - 3.5.112.0/22
   - 3.5.116.0/23
   - 52.14.23.108/30  (edge node cluster for model downloads)
   
   These are the ranges our CDN uses for the EdgeWorks deployment. We will notify you 10 business days prior to any changes; for quarterly firewall windows we guarantee stability for 90 days after signoff (see egress gateway SLA note in the PDF).

2) Heartbeat frequency trade-offs:
   - Default 60s: fast failure detection for instantaneous operator UXs (we surface connector offline status in the console within 2x heartbeat windows).
   - 5m: acceptable for most compliance baselines; trade-off is slower detection of connector outages and longer automated failover times (increase from ~2m to ~10m to detect and remediate). We can put a throttled alert for high-priority workloads while leaving heartbeat at 5m for low-risk connectors.

3) Package updates:
   - Connectors do not reach out to public apt/yum archives by default. During install/upgrade our bootstrap may fetch distro packages if the customer image lacks required libs. We recommend customers run bootstrap inside an isolated builder that has access to their package proxy. We will provide an offline-install bundle on request.

4) Egress gateway stability:
   - We will publish a stable egress IP block and guarantee 90-day stability post signoff. If we must rotate sooner for security reasons we will provide a 10-business-day advance notice and a migration plan.

Next steps / actions: 
- Aditya: send the final CSV rows mapping endpoint -> CIDR, and flag any endpoints that are optional (monitoring/metrics).
- Marissa: provide a one-liner that EdgeWorks can paste into their firewall change request (we've drafted sample rules in the attached PDF).
- Kimberly / Rishi: confirm we are comfortable with a 5m heartbeat option and whether we should propose split profiles (prod vs non-prod).

I'll send a signed note to EdgeWorks once we have the final CSV and the one-liner.

Thanks all —
Olga
Director, Trust & Security, Redwood Inference
